likely_causes: Boost leak at charge air cooler hose or clamp|Restricted air filter|Variable geometry turbo actuator sticking|Failed turbocharger|Exhaust leak before the turbine
advisor_guidance: Engine is not making the boost it is commanding. Usually a leak in the charge air plumbing rather than the turbo itself. Expect a pressure test before any turbo work is quoted.

likely_causes: Boost leak|VGT actuator fault|Boost pressure sensor drift|Soot fouling of the VGT vanes
advisor_guidance: Related to P0299 and usually caused by the same leak. Diagnose the two together.

likely_causes: Failing ignition coil|Worn spark plugs|Vacuum leak|Low fuel pressure|Low compression|Contaminated fuel
advisor_guidance: The engine is misfiring on more than one cylinder. Safe to drive a short distance but sustained driving can damage the catalytic converter. Should be seen promptly.

likely_causes: Ignition coil on cylinder 1|Spark plug on cylinder 1|Fuel injector on cylinder 1|Low compression on cylinder 1
advisor_guidance: A specific cylinder is misfiring. Usually a coil or plug on that cylinder.

likely_causes: Ignition coil on cylinder 2|Spark plug on cylinder 2|Fuel injector on cylinder 2|Low compression on cylinder 2
advisor_guidance: A specific cylinder is misfiring. Usually a coil or plug on that cylinder.

likely_causes: Ignition coil on cylinder 3|Spark plug on cylinder 3|Fuel injector on cylinder 3|Low compression on cylinder 3
advisor_guidance: A specific cylinder is misfiring. Usually a coil or plug on that cylinder.

likely_causes: Ignition coil on cylinder 4|Spark plug on cylinder 4|Fuel injector on cylinder 4|Low compression on cylinder 4
advisor_guidance: A specific cylinder is misfiring. Usually a coil or plug on that cylinder.

description: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold bank 1
likely_causes: Aged or failed catalytic converter|Exhaust leak upstream of the rear oxygen sensor|Failed rear oxygen sensor|Unresolved engine misfire damaging the catalyst
advisor_guidance: The catalytic converter is not cleaning the exhaust as well as it should. Not an immediate driveability problem but it will fail an emissions test.

likely_causes: Carbon-blocked EGR passages|Stuck EGR valve|Failed differential pressure sensor|Blocked EGR cooler
advisor_guidance: EGR flow is restricted, usually by carbon buildup. Common on vehicles doing short urban routes.

likely_causes: Failed TCC solenoid|Wiring fault to the solenoid|Low or contaminated transmission fluid|Internal torque converter fault
advisor_guidance: The torque converter lockup circuit has a fault. Have the fluid condition checked before anything internal is quoted.

description: Torque converter clutch circuit performance or stuck off
likely_causes: Contaminated or wrong-specification transmission fluid|Failed TCC solenoid|Worn torque converter clutch friction material|Valve body wear
advisor_guidance: Lockup is not engaging as commanded. Wrong transmission fluid is a common and inexpensive cause worth ruling out first.

likely_causes: Intermittent wiring or connector fault|TCC solenoid beginning to fail|Fluid temperature sensor fault
advisor_guidance: An intermittent fault in the lockup circuit. May come and go with temperature.

likely_causes: DEF tank low or empty|DEF level sensor fault|Contaminated DEF affecting the sensor reading
advisor_guidance: DEF is low or the system thinks it is. If the tank is genuinely full the sensor or the DEF quality is the issue. Derate follows if it is not addressed.

likely_causes: Contaminated or diluted DEF|DEF aged beyond shelf life|Diesel cross-contamination in the DEF supply|NOx sensor drift
advisor_guidance: The DEF does not meet specification. Test the customer's bulk DEF supply as well as the vehicle - if the bulk tank is the source every vehicle refilled from it will return.

description: Diesel particulate filter efficiency below threshold bank 1
likely_causes: Ash-loaded DPF requiring cleaning|Damaged or cracked DPF substrate|Differential pressure sensor or hose fault|Repeated incomplete regenerations
advisor_guidance: The particulate filter is not performing. Often ash loading on a vehicle doing short routes rather than a failed part.

description: Diesel particulate filter restriction - ash accumulation
likely_causes: Ash accumulation at service interval|Excessive oil consumption loading the filter with ash|Incorrect engine oil specification (high ash)
advisor_guidance: Ash does not burn off in a regeneration and eventually needs the filter physically cleaned. This is a scheduled service item, not a failure.

description: Lost communication with body control module
likely_causes: Failed or sleeping module|CAN bus wiring fault|Low system voltage from a discharged battery|Module software fault
advisor_guidance: A module stopped talking on the network. Frequently a symptom of low battery voltage rather than a module failure - check the charging and draw first.

likely_causes: Failing alternator|Loose or corroded battery cables|Failed battery|Excessive parasitic draw|Slipping accessory drive belt
advisor_guidance: System voltage is below normal. Could be charging or could be a draw flattening the battery overnight.

likely_causes: Failed voltage regulator|Failed alternator|Poor ground connection at the regulator
advisor_guidance: Charging voltage is too high, which will damage the battery and electronics. Should not be driven far.

description: Left front wheel speed sensor circuit
likely_causes: Damaged wheel speed sensor|Wiring damage at the wheel|Debris or corrosion on the tone ring|Failed ABS module input
advisor_guidance: The ABS cannot read one wheel's speed. ABS and stability control will be disabled but normal braking still works.

description: Right front wheel speed sensor circuit
likely_causes: Damaged wheel speed sensor|Wiring damage at the wheel|Debris or corrosion on the tone ring|Failed ABS module input
advisor_guidance: The ABS cannot read one wheel's speed. ABS and stability control will be disabled but normal braking still works.

likely_causes: Sensor not calibrated after an alignment|Failed steering angle sensor|Clockspring fault
advisor_guidance: Stability control needs to know where the steering is pointed. Often just needs recalibrating after alignment work.

likely_causes: Thermostat stuck open|Failed coolant temperature sensor|Low coolant level
advisor_guidance: The engine is taking too long to warm up. Usually a stuck thermostat. Hurts fuel economy and cabin heat.

likely_causes: Vacuum leak|Failed or dirty mass air flow sensor|Weak fuel pump|Restricted fuel filter|Leaking intake manifold gasket
advisor_guidance: The engine is running lean. Commonly an unmetered air leak.

likely_causes: Restricted fuel filter|Failing high pressure fuel pump|Water in fuel|Leaking injector return
advisor_guidance: Fuel pressure is below what the engine needs. On a diesel, check the fuel filter and water separator first.

likely_causes: Fuel pressure regulator fault|Failed rail pressure sensor|Restricted fuel return line
advisor_guidance: Fuel pressure is above specification. Should be seen promptly.

likely_causes: Discharged battery|Failed charging system|Parasitic draw|Corroded battery terminals
advisor_guidance: A module is reporting low battery voltage. Check charging and parasitic draw before replacing the battery.

description: Evaporative emission system leak detected - gross leak
likely_causes: Loose or missing fuel cap|Cracked EVAP hose|Failed purge or vent valve|Damaged fuel filler neck
advisor_guidance: Often just a loose fuel cap. Worth checking that before anything else is quoted.

description: Evaporative emission system leak detected - small leak
likely_causes: Small EVAP hose crack|Failed vent valve seal|Degraded fuel cap seal
advisor_guidance: A small leak in the fuel vapour system. Not a driveability problem but it will fail emissions.
